skills.name: Demo brief
skills.detail: Loads demand, lane, cost, capacity, and resilience assumptions.

skills.name: cuOpt skill
skills.detail: Solves routing and load assignment across Taiwan manufacturing nodes.

skills.name: Vision Insights
skills.detail: Uses Nemotron Omni to interpret charts generated from the optimized plan.

skills.name: AIQ Research
skills.detail: Produces a research-backed business plan with risks and competitive context.

vision.codex: Nemotron Omni flags the optimized plan as more balanced: Hsinchu and Tainan move out of the critical band, air freight drops below the stress threshold, and buffer capacity becomes usable for demand spikes.
vision.claude: Nemotron Omni reads the chart as a meaningful utilization shift: the optimized assignment lowers peak stress at Hsinchu and Tainan while preserving enough buffer for late-stage expedite requests.

strategy.summary: The optimized network should be positioned as a resilient premium manufacturing corridor anchored by Hsinchu wafer supply, Taichung precision components, Tainan advanced packaging, and flexible Kaohsiung export capacity.
points: Use cuOpt output as the operating plan for weekly production commitments and exception handling.
Package the route economics as a partner-facing proof point for CUDA-X accelerated planning.
Treat Taiwan routing resilience as the differentiator, not only cost reduction.

market.summary: The strongest buyer profile is an advanced electronics manufacturer that needs faster plan refresh, constrained supplier coordination, and auditable tradeoffs across cost, cycle time, and capacity risk.
points: Compete against spreadsheet planning, generic supply-chain suites, and isolated operations research tooling.
Lead with accelerated solve time and packaged agent skills that turn optimization into business decisions.
Use GTC Taipei as the venue for partner validation with manufacturers, logistics providers, and systems integrators.

risk.summary: The plan is feasible if it treats route optimization as a decision support layer and keeps geopolitical, weather, capacity, and supplier constraints visible to operators.
points: Maintain alternate port and air-freight lanes for typhoon season and port congestion events.
Require human approval for material changes to priority lots, supplier allocations, or customer commitments.
Track data freshness, supplier SLA quality, and exception drift as production readiness gates.

execution.summary: A credible pilot can start with weekly planning data, then expand into daily re-optimization, AIQ-backed market updates, and Vision Insights reviews of operational dashboards.
points: Phase one: run cuOpt on historical and current weekly demand to validate savings and service levels.
Phase two: attach Vision Insights to planning dashboards for chart interpretation and anomaly triage.
Phase three: trigger AIQ Research reports for board-level business planning and partner strategy.
